title: Raising the Collection Charge for a Palletised Freight Run on Renew Business Asset Buyback
content:
A palletised collection on a Renew Business Asset Buyback agreement is charged to the profile when the run is booked, that is while the agreement is still waiting for machines to be collected and none has been booked in on it; a collection on any other Renew programme, and a batch already booked in, carry no collection charge under this rule.

**What the charge does to the account.** One entry is booked against the agreement recording what the retailer charges the customer for sending the carrier to collect the machines, and the freight and handling still owed on the agreement is increased by that amount. The customer sees the charge listed against the trade-in agreement and carried on their account until it is settled or waived.

**Raising it.** The charge is raised through `charge_collection_freight_530ef4f1`, which the desk unlocks and calls itself; the entry is the retailer's own booking on the profile's trade-in account.

**What the entry takes.**

- `tradein_agreement_id` — Id class. The reference number of the Renew trade-in agreement the collection is run under, read from the trade-in agreement record found for the customer profile.
- `customer_id` — Id class. The customer reference number of the profile being charged, read from the customer profile record.
- `handling_fee_amount` — Fixed-format class. The amount charged for the collection, in USD to 2 decimal places, rounded half up at the cent when it is booked, and never negative.

**What comes back.** A confirmation line in plain text naming the charge entry booked, the agreement it was booked against, the amount charged in USD and the freight and handling now outstanding on the agreement. The line being returned is what shows the charge is booked, and the entry can then be read back among the agreement's trade-in history entries.
